item.title: How to get rid of unwanted AI on your phone
item.description: Google AI Overviews can't be permanently turned off, but adding -AI to your searches and using the built-in Web filter can help bypass AI summaries.
item.content:encoded:
You pull out your phone to look something up on Google. Maybe you're researching a purchase or trying to find a restaurant. You expect a list of websites. Instead, Google serves up a lengthy artificial intelligence-generated answer before you even get to the search results. Sound familiar? I like AI when it helps me get something done. But sometimes I just want to search the internet without an AI summary appearing every time.

Fortunately, there are ways around it. One involves adding a few characters to your search. Another uses a built-in Google filter. And if you've had enough of Siri suggestions on your iPhone or AI features popping up on your Samsung Galaxy or Google Pixel, there are settings worth changing there, too.

Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money

In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com.

HOW TO SEARCH ANYTHING ON IPHONE, GALAXY AND PIXEL

Google calls those automatically generated summaries AI Overviews. They appear above traditional search results when Google's systems decide an AI-generated answer might be helpful. Sometimes they save time. However, they can also get in the way when you'd rather read information directly from a website. Unfortunately, Google confirms that AI Overviews cannot be permanently turned off through a standard Search setting. However, you have a few ways to avoid them.

This trick takes only seconds and is worth trying on an iPhone, iPad, Samsung Galaxy or Google Pixel.

Here's how.

For example, instead of searching for: best walking shoes

Try: best walking shoes -AI

Adding -AI can keep an AI Overview from appearing. However, this is an unofficial workaround, and Google doesn't guarantee that it will work every time. There's another catch. Google uses the minus sign to exclude terms from search results. Adding -AI could also remove some relevant pages containing that term. If the trick doesn't work, Google's next option is more dependable.

Google has a built-in filter that shows traditional web links without AI Overviews.

Here's how to find it.

Google will display text-based links without its AI Overview. The downside is that you generally need to select the Web filter again when starting another search. Still, it's a useful way to get straight to websites without an AI-generated answer taking up the top of the screen.

One important note: Turning off an AI Overviews experiment in Google Search Labs won't necessarily remove AI Overviews from regular Google searches.

If you're really tired of AI showing up in searches, there's another option worth knowing about. DuckDuckGo offers a dedicated search experience called DuckDuckGo No-AI. You can access it at noai.duckduckgo.com. According to DuckDuckGo, this version removes its AI-assisted answers and AI feature suggestions. It also filters AI-generated images from image searches. The company acknowledges that AI-image filtering may not catch everything. You can use the website directly without changing your phone's default search engine.

If you want to use a different search engine more regularly, Apple makes switching easy.

These instructions apply to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27.

Keep in mind that choosing regular DuckDuckGo as your default doesn't automatically activate its separate No-AI experience. You can visit the No-AI website whenever you want to use it.

MALICIOUS BROWSER EXTENSIONS CAN HIJACK AI ASSISTANTS

Now let's talk about another feature that can get annoying. Ever swipe down on your iPhone's Home Screen to search for something and immediately see a collection of suggested apps? Those suggestions come from Siri, which can recommend apps based on your activity. Maybe you appreciate the shortcuts. Or maybe you would rather see a clean search screen until you start typing. Apple lets you turn those suggestions off.

Your iPhone should stop showing those suggested apps before you begin searching. While you're there, you can also disable Show in App Library if you don't want suggestions appearing there. You can turn off Show When Sharing if you'd rather not see suggested contacts or other Siri recommendations when sharing content. These controls change where Siri suggestions appear. They don't disable Siri itself.

Apple's more conversational Siri AI is available in beta on supported iPhones running iOS 27.

If you enabled it and would rather return to the previous Siri experience, Apple provides that option.

If you don't want to use Siri at all, leave it turned off.

Important: Siri AI requires an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone, including the iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max and iPhone 16 models or later. Availability also depends on language and region. Older iPhones won't have the same Siri AI options.

There's another AI feature that may bother some iPhone owners. Apple Intelligence can summarize notifications, messages and emails. While that may sound convenient, AI summaries can leave out details or misunderstand what someone wrote. If you'd rather read the original text, you can disable those features.

Turn off AI notification summaries

Disable AI summaries in Messages

You can also open Settings, tap Apps, select Mail and turn off Summarize Message Previews.

These options are available on compatible devices running iOS 27. Disabling them won't affect your ability to receive regular messages or notifications.

Samsung has been adding AI tools to its Galaxy phones, including features that help with calls or photos. Some can be useful. However, you may have no interest in having AI analyze information or suggest actions throughout your day. Fortunately, Samsung provides individual controls for many Galaxy AI features.

Samsung notes that some AI features are built into the operating system and cannot be disabled. Also, available controls vary depending on your Galaxy model and software version. Samsung recommends restarting your device after disabling Galaxy AI features to ensure the changes take effect.

Samsung's Now brief can show personalized information about your day, including upcoming events and other recommendations. If you don't want those briefings appearing on your Lock screen, try this.

You can also open Settings, tap Galaxy AI and select Now brief to adjust the information included in your briefings. On supported devices, you can disable Show Now brief while phone is locked. Keep in mind that removing Now brief from the Lock screen doesn't necessarily remove the feature from your Galaxy phone.

If you're concerned about information being sent to the cloud for AI processing, Samsung offers another option.

This tells supported Samsung Galaxy AI features to process data locally instead of using cloud processing. However, some AI features require an internet connection and may become unavailable. Also, this control applies to Samsung's supported Galaxy AI features. It doesn't prevent every app on your phone from connecting to its own cloud services.

Circle to Search lets you search for something displayed on your screen. However, you might accidentally activate it while navigating your phone.

You can switch it off.

Google Pixel phones have their own AI features designed to anticipate what you might need. Depending on your device, these can include Magic Cue or Google's newer Proactive Assistance. Both can provide suggestions using information from supported apps, depending on your settings and permissions. However, you may prefer to keep those suggestions out of your conversations.

On supported Pixel 10 models, Magic Cue can display helpful information while you're using your phone. For example, it might surface flight details during a conversation.

Here's how to adjust it.

Magic Cue is available only on supported Pixel models and in supported regions.

Google introduced a newer feature called Proactive Assistance on Pixel 11 devices in supported markets, including the United States. When enabled, it can use screen information and notifications to provide suggestions. It may also use information from connected apps and location data.

If you'd rather skip those suggestions, Google gives you a direct switch.

You can also tap Connected apps to decide which apps the feature can access. Proactive Assistance is opt-in, so you won't necessarily see suggestions unless you've enabled it.

Circle to Search is also available on supported Pixel phones. If you find yourself activating it accidentally, you can turn it off.

Google also lists the feature under System on supported Pixel devices.

On supported Pixel phones, the Pixel Screenshots app can generate summaries and help you search through saved screenshots. If you don't want those AI features processing screenshot content, Google provides an option to disable them.

If you also want to delete previously generated AI information, select Delete all AI summaries and metadata. That last option removes the generated summaries and metadata associated with the feature. Only select it if you're comfortable deleting that information.

ANTI-SCAM SETTINGS ON IPHONE, PIXEL AND GALAXY YOU SHOULD CHECK

Finally, there's Gemini, Google's AI assistant. On many Android phones, Gemini can launch when you say "Hey Google" or press and hold the power button. If you're tired of activating it accidentally, there are several ways to stop that behavior.

Turn off Hey Google in Gemini

This prevents Gemini from responding to the wake phrase. You can still open the app manually if you want to use it.

On Google Pixel and other supported Android phones:

On Samsung Galaxy phones, search Settings for Side button to find the equivalent shortcut control.

If you'd rather stop using Gemini as your phone's main assistant, Google provides another option.

You can also switch back to Google Assistant through the Gemini app on supported devices. Removing Gemini as the default assistant won't necessarily uninstall the Gemini app or erase any previous Gemini activity.

There isn't one universal switch that removes every AI feature from an iPhone or Android device. Some functions are built directly into the software. Others come from individual apps or online services.

However, you can make a noticeable difference by disabling the features you never use. And remember, turning off an AI assistant won't automatically remove AI Overviews from Google Search. Those require separate controls. If you're concerned about how AI services collect information, we've also covered how to opt out of AI data collection in popular apps.

I use AI regularly, and I appreciate what it can do. But I also understand why people get annoyed when it starts showing up everywhere. Sometimes I want to Google something and read what an actual person wrote. I don't need an AI summary making that decision for me. That's why I like having Google's Web filter available. And discovering DuckDuckGo's No-AI search option gives people another choice. I also think it's worth taking a few minutes to look at the AI settings on your phone. You may discover features running that you never use. Turning them off can make your phone feel more like your own again. I want AI available when I need it, but I don't want companies deciding that I need it all the time.

Are Apple, Google and Samsung giving us useful AI features, or are they pushing the technology so aggressively that we're losing control of our own phones? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Paige Spiranac leaves her fans speechless with 'fall golf' content series, Raiders fan fight & hot dog prices
item.description: Screencaps, America's Best Daily Column, covers Paige Spiranac's fall golf bat signal, golf cart heaters, and Costco hand warmers for cold rounds.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers. Screencaps, which publishes seven-days-a-week, is a mix of sports, pop culture, and emails from sane readers from around the world. This column isn't for the coastal elites. Give us a week to steal your heart. Our track record is pretty good. Let's have some fun.

Personally, I didn't need any influencing, but now that Paigeviews has officially dumped out fall golf content, I suddenly feel the urge to play MORE fall golf. There's something about those cold mornings with a buddy in a golf cart where you're both hacking up a lung after a long night of drinking and watching college football as the sun shines off the fairway dew.

There's something about getting out the golf cart seat blanket that I bought for those cold mornings. My buddy Diesel even figured out a way to hotwire a space heater to golf cart battery terminals so he can keep his cart warm. This guy even has a steering wheel cover that he'll break out to keep his hands warm.

When it's real cold, like Thanksgiving Eve, Diesel will get that space heater and put a cover over his cart and turn it into a hot box. It'll be 41 and chilly outside while 78 and tropical inside his cart.

The beauty of fall golf is the challenge. How long into winter can we go? We've played in SE Michigan on December 23. A pond on the course was frozen solid. But, the golf was good. The greens were rolling fairly smooth.

Paige's content this morning was a bat signal. It's a reminder that us men must do whatever it takes to breathe that fresh air before winter crushes our soul. Get your heaters out. Get your hand warmers from Costco – Lil Hotties – and get out there and play real golf before going indoors where you'll shoot in the 70s and think you're really good.

Thank you for your service, Paige.

PAIGE SPIRANAC & FORMER PELOTON INSTRUCTOR SHOW WOMEN HOW TO TEE A GOLF BALL, NHL FAN FIGHT & DUMP DINNERS

📩 Email: joe.kinsey@outkick.com
Send photos, stories, tips, rants—whatever you've got.

Speaking of fall golf, I know this is going to make Ohio State fans puke, but I did go up with Canoe Kirk and a couple of other golf buddies to play Radrick Farms, a University of Michigan course. Beautiful course. Incredible design from Pete Dye.

Here's what surprised me: If there wasn't a sign at the road announcing it was a University of Michigan property, you wouldn't know it. Arriving at the clubhouse, there are no signs that I saw mentioning the school. The golf carts don't have massive 'M' logos on the side. They're not even yellow. Not even a yellow stripe. The tee boxes aren't Michigan branded. The golf cart tees they provide aren't Michigan branded. The scorecard had a 'M' on the front, but the M was face down on the scorecard clip.

PAIGE SPIRANAC NEEDS TO EMBRACE FULL INTEGRITY GOLF AFTER PUTTING INCIDENT, TRUMP'S NEW HIRE & DITKA!

I shot a full integrity 44-44 with 38 putts from 6,000 yards. No gimmes. I will have nightmares over No. 16. I reached in two and had a putt for eagle only to spray it way wide right. Three putt par.

For those of you keeping track, the last three courses I've played have been all private. It's time to get back to slumming it a little bit.

• Michael V. in Florida emails: I have watched College Gameday for many years and was very hesitant about Pat McAfee replacing Lee Corso. Like just about any fan of the show I was a big fan of Corso even though he had a lot of trouble speaking the last few years. That being said, I do enjoy some of what McAfee has brought to the show. He is a little over the top sometimes but his enthusiasm seems genuine and he is not afraid to say and do things that ESPN doesnt agree with. The kicking contest every week is also entertaining. The show will.never be the same without the head gear pick but I still enjoy it.

• Ryan F. tells on himself: My guy, you work for a content farm. I used to enjoy Fox sports articles before Outkick came along and now it's all poorly written tripe with a clear agenda of national division, just like this article. Please retire from writing and do something better with your life.

Kinsey: I guarantee Ryan liked the narrative that the cops were called on the 3-year-old kid for being "too good" that the parents pushed. Ryan clearly didn't like that I went out and contacted the Winter Park police to get the real story of what's going on here: The parents are a pain in the ass.

Ryan wanted me to explain where parents are supposed to send a 3 year old for soccer in Orlando. It turns out Paris Saint-Germain runs an academy for 4U kids in town. You know, the famous PSG club where other prodigies are training.

COPS CALLED TO FLORIDA YOUTH SOCCER GAME TO DEAL WITH PARENTS OF 3-YEAR-OLD SOCCER PRODIGY

But...but...but...it's expensive! The family could've shown up at the door with their kid and PSG would figure out a way to work with their finances. The kid is that good. You don't think PSG wouldn't want him in their club? Shame on Ryan for being such a LIB moron.

• Rick in Sanger, TX asks: The youth league soccer director knew the kid was too good last season, why did they allow him to compete with three-year-olds again?

Kinsey: I emailed i9 Sports asking questions about the incident and for the organization to provide some clarity. They still have not responded to those questions. My guess is that i9 is terrified of banning any kid from playing, but once the parents became a total pain in the ass, then they had grounds for removal. Were the parents a pain in the ass in the spring/summer? We don't know.

• Joyce complains: My granddaughter was put on a 6u team. She missed the cut off date for the next level up (8u) by 12 days. We warned everyone that she was a good player since she had attended a few soccer clinics the last couple of years.  She ended up dribbling around everyone scoring at least 5 or 6 goals in the first 5 minutes of the game.

After a couple of games she was told to play in the back field and pass it to the other kids so they could score goals. That was okay for part of the game but not the whole game each week. It was like she was being punished for being a good player and she had just turned 6 years old. They clearly did not want her scoring goals. As a result, We have to get her back in the soccer clinics for her to get her skills back to where they were.  All of that and not to mention my dad was one of the original founders of the AYSO. I’m sure that’s not what they intended. Needless to say we will be switching to club soccer as soon as she’s old enough!

Kinsey: Find better clubs. There are plenty of clubs out there that will take your money at the 6U level.

• Another Joyce emailed: I’ve coached youth sports for years. I cannot believe the parent! If the kid was fouling every kid wouldn’t he  be given a red card from the referee, not a jelly parent? I was in trouble when my team beat the other team really bad and we were holding back, they threatened to disband my team! It’s all about everyone gets a trophy.

• Jason DeM. fires back: Whoa whoa whoa, pump the breaks a little bit bro…. "To me making it a performance is all about the singer making it more about them then the Anthem itself. Which is no different than taking a knee."

You’re joking right? You’re comparing a talented singer putting a slight variation into their rendition of the National Anthem to scumbags who protest it? Not even close to being the same thing.

Also, I’m a vet as well and Gary doesn’t speak for all who proudly served.

Having said that, I think this young lady did a fine job but doesn’t hold a candle to Whitney or even Chris Stapleton’s Super Bowl anthem.

Did Big Plastic have some sort of deal with Big Cereal to make us go like 75 years without innovation?

• Dean in Wisconsin emails: No!  Never!  Not if I can have any say in it!  I don’t trust my local Kroger affiliate to have their employees pick my food out for me.  I worked in grocery stores almost a half -century ago when I was a college student and I wouldn’t have trusted my fellow employees to "shop" for me then! 

I want to "eye ball" any and all fresh fruits and vegetables as well as check the sell by dates on meats, dairy products, and breads – I always go with the date that is the farthest into the future.  Would I trust a grocery store employee to do that?  Hell, no!  I would expect to get a gall on of milk that has a sell by date of the day I picked it up if I let the store employee pick it out for me. 

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

There is an employee at my local Kroger affiliate who does the shopping for online customers who I call "Co usin Itt" .  Cousin Itt was a character on the "Addams Family" TV show whose hair covered his face and body entirely .  This employee has hair that covers his entire face, sort of like Cousin Itt .   Yes, you can’t see this guy’s face.   I have no idea how he sees anything .   The one time I did partially see his face, it was covered in body piercings.  Would I trust him to do grocery shopping for me?   Umm, no.

• Bob K. checks in: There is no way I am trusting anyone to pick out my food.  My wife hates grocery shopping , so every week I look at the Publix specials ( BOGO’s ) and make my plan and go to Publix every Saturday and do the shopping, ( I sometimes even put a pineapple upside down in my cart, if you know you know ) just to see if I get any reactions.  Not to be disrespectful, but I see the people who are doing grocery deliveries in the store and no way in H E double hockey sticks am I going to trust them to touch my food, pick out my food, put it in their vehicle and bring it to my house, just not happening.

#################

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

That is it for a MASSIVE edition. I love the passionate emails and conversation. There's plenty more piled up to get to. As for today, I have a sports experience planned for tonight that I've had on my radar for the last 6-8 weeks. More on that tomorrow morning.

Let's get the day rolling. Go have a great one.

item.title: Leftist streamer triggers fury after mocking 'funny' injuries to ICE agents at Ilhan Omar event: ‘Disgusting’
item.description: Hasan Piker mocked injured ICE agents during a Minneapolis campaign event with Rep. Ilhan Omar, drawing swift condemnation from conservatives.
item.content:encoded:
Far-left streamer Hasan Piker sparked online controversy after he mocked the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents injured in Operation Metro Surge during a campaign event alongside Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., Monday night.

Recalling his time in Minnesota amid protests over the Trump administration’s federal immigration crackdown, Piker said he thought agents must be "extra racist" to be out in frigid winter temperatures and mocked one of them who was injured as the crowd laughed along.

"We saw a lot of funny compilations as well, you know. A lot of hip bones were broken. 'Officer Martinez down,'" he said while speaking to Democratic socialist and failed Minneapolis mayoral candidate Omar Fateh, who hosted the sold-out Minneapolis event.

Piker has joined several prominent Democrats on their campaign trails, emerging as a polarizing figure within the Democratic Party that some are embracing while others are rejecting. He has made national headlines for past rhetoric, including his claim that "America deserved 9/11," and has faced accusations of antisemitism over his remarks on Israel and Hamas.

ILHAN OMAR'S RADICAL STREAMER ALLY RALLIES WITH EMBATTLED LAWMAKER AFTER DC HOME RAID

Omar, who shared the stage with Piker that night, has been immersed in controversy of her own after Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents searched her Washington, D.C., home earlier this month and a federal court filing identified the congresswoman as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, aka Ilhan Abdullahi Omar."

Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., and Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., publicly condemned Piker, while other Minnesota Democrats called for the event to be canceled as voters prepare to head to the polls ahead of next week’s midterm elections. Omar’s campaign backed her decision to attend to mobilize young voters.

Piker also told Fateh that he was inspired by the "solidarity" and "mutual aid" following the deployment of thousands of ICE and Customs and Border Protection agents to Minnesota. Protests resulted in multiple arrests, objects and fireworks thrown at law enforcement and the disruption of a church service. Two U.S. citizens, Renée Good and Alex Pretti, were killed during interactions with federal law enforcement.

ILHAN OMAR JOINS 'POLARIZING AND DANGEROUS' STREAMER AT CAMPAIGN EVENT DESPITE DEMOCRATIC BACKLASH

"It wasn’t just the networks that were very quickly propped up, the mutual aid that I saw, the protests that sparked up that said, ‘We’re not going to take it. We’re not going to sit aside and watch this administration come and rip our communities apart and kidnap our neighbors,'" he said.

Piker, who streams his commentary on Twitch, called Republicans "terrorists" during the event, and Omar referred to the party as the "pedophile protection party."

Conservatives on social media quickly condemned Piker's comments.

"Hasan Piker was asked what stuck with him from Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis: ‘Funny compilations’ of federal agents being injured," Charlie Kirk Show executive producer Andrew Kolvet posted on X. "He also called the agents ‘extra racist.’ This isn’t comedy. It’s tacit support for the far-left insurrection network against federal law enforcement. Pro-revolution. Pro-anarchy."

"Every Democrat he campaigned with should be asked if they agree. Disgusting."

"Hasan and his elected Democrats are sick," Loomer Unleashed posted on X.

HASAN PIKER LASHES OUT AT REPUBLICANS, CALLS THEM 'TERRORISTS' IN EVENT WITH ILHAN OMAR

In another post on X, Crucible Updates wrote, "Hasan watched federal agents get hurt and his takeaway was 'funny compilations… a lot of hip bones were broken.' Millions of young women take their politics from this guy. Let that sink in."

"WTF?!" Gina Milan, a conservative media personality, posted on X.

"This guy is America’s biggest cancer. Just another Nepo baby," Kevin Smith, host of Loud Majority Live, posted on X.

A Department of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital that the "vilification" of ICE agents who "put their lives on the line" every day to enforce the law is contributing to a more than 1,600% increase in assaults against them.

"They should be thanking our law enforcement for removing these dangerous criminals from Minnesota—NOT vilifying law enforcement," the spokesperson wrote. "While these people smear ICE, law enforcement is arresting criminals and saving countless American lives."

The spokesperson added that ICE agents do not target individuals based on skin color and take required steps to determine immigration status and removability before making an arrest.

"Politicians and activists must turn the temperature down and tone down their rhetoric," the spokesperson wrote.

Omar is running against former state trooper John Nagel and independent candidate DeVelle Jackson in the upcoming midterm elections for Minnesota’s 5th Congressional District.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker and Omar for comment.

item.title: LEE CARTER: America is angry at everyone — but who will actually vote?
item.description: Democrats lead midterm election polls, but the gap narrows sharply among voters certain to participate, making voter turnout the key factor.
item.content:encoded:
America is furious.

Democrats are furious at Trump. Republicans are furious at Democrats. Independents are furious at just about everyone.

At last, something we can agree on.

INDEPENDENT VOTERS AREN’T PICKING A POLITICAL TEAM, THEY JUST FEEL PICKED ON

With just under a week until the midterms, Americans are being told that everything is at stake. Democracy. The economy. Our freedoms. The future of the country itself.

And yet, according to AP-NORC polling, only about two in 10 voters believe either political party is strongly focused on helping people like them or capable of solving important problems.

We've never been told an election matters more. We've rarely expected less from the people we're electing.

So here's the question I've been thinking about as a pollster.

LEE CARTER: THE SUMMER POLLS MISSED THE POINT: VOTERS ARE MOVING — AND THE MIDTERMS BEGIN

What happens when everyone is angry, but not everyone is angry enough to vote?

Because that's what makes this election so difficult to predict.

We spend an enormous amount of time asking Americans whom they support. But in a midterm election, the more important question may be whether they care enough to show up.

And the latest polling suggests those are two very different things.

TRUMP VOTERS REVEAL THEIR BIGGEST FEAR HEADING INTO MIDTERMS — AND IT'S NOT RISING PRICES

A CNBC survey found that 74% of Democrats worry President Donald Trump will exceed his constitutional authority if Republicans retain control of Congress. Meanwhile, 54% of Republicans fear Democrats will enact democratic socialist policies.

Those aren't equivalent concerns, or equally intense ones. But they tell us something important about the electorate.

Democrats fear a president with too much power. Republicans fear a government with too much reach.

Both sides have plenty to be angry about.

DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING. HERE ARE 3 FORCES THAT COULD STOP IT

But anger doesn't vote. People do.

And here's where things get interesting.

Research examining the 2018 midterms found that worry helped predict who actually voted. Enthusiasm did not show the same relationship.

Remember 2018? Nearly half of eligible Americans voted, the highest midterm turnout in more than a century.

Apparently, Americans don't necessarily need to love their candidates to get themselves to the polls. Sometimes worrying about the alternative is motivation enough.

Which brings us to 2026.

Pew Research finds Democrats have a substantial motivation advantage. Among voters who say they're extremely motivated, Democrats lead Republicans by 24 points.

If those were the only people voting, Democrats could start planning a very enjoyable election night.

But look at a different group.

Among people who actually voted in both 2022 and 2024, the Democratic advantage is just six points.

That's an enormous difference.

The people who say they're most motivated to vote aren't necessarily the same people with the strongest history of showing up.

And that's a distinction worth remembering before anyone starts declaring a landslide.

The latest Fox News poll gives Democrats a 54% to 45% advantage on the generic congressional ballot. But among voters certain to participate, that lead narrows to six points.

CBS News projects Democrats will win 229 House seats, enough to reclaim the majority.

But CBS has identified another complication.

Democrats have more voters who say they're definitely voting or have already voted. Republicans have more voters who say they might vote.

In other words, Democrats have more of the voters who say they're coming. Republicans have more of the voters who haven't decided whether to bother.

And that may be the most important political question of the next week.

Will those Republicans show up? Will they stay home? Will something happen in the final days that convinces them this election matters?

Nobody knows for certain.

And in a closely divided House, the answer could determine who controls Congress.

This is why polling is both enormously useful and endlessly frustrating.

We can measure what Americans think with considerable precision.

Predicting what they'll actually do is harder.

In fact, one of the most revealing findings from Pew's analysis of the 2022 midterms is that Republican gains were driven largely by differences in turnout, not a great wave of voters changing their minds.

Among Americans who voted in both 2020 and 2022, very few switched parties.

What changed was who showed up.

Seventy-one percent of Trump's 2020 voters participated in the 2022 midterms, compared with 67% of Biden's 2020 voters.

Four points.

Not exactly the stuff of dramatic campaign commercials.

But across millions of voters, a few points can change the outcome of an election.

Sometimes elections aren't decided because Americans change their minds. They're decided because different Americans show up.

And suddenly, a few things about this campaign begin to make more sense.

Take Trump's whistle-stop tour.

Why is a sitting president spending the final days of a midterm campaign racing from rally to rally when his approval ratings are so low?

Because Republicans may not need him to change many minds. They need him to get the right people out of the house.

Trump has demonstrated an unusual ability to attract voters who don't always participate in elections. The challenge for Republicans is getting those voters to show up when Trump himself isn't on the ballot.

A rally may not change someone's opinion of the president. But it might change whether that person votes.

And in a close election, that's worth considerably more than another favorable headline.

Then consider something that has received surprisingly little attention: voter registration.

Since 2018, the party-registration balance has shifted toward Republicans by roughly eight points in North Carolina, seven in Pennsylvania, five in Nevada and four in Arizona.

Those aren't election results. Registering Republican doesn't mean someone will vote Republican, and it certainly doesn't guarantee they'll vote at all.

But the shifts suggest the pool of potential voters has changed.

And that matters enormously when turnout is the great unknown.

Democrats may have an advantage among voters who say they're highly motivated. Republicans may have a larger reservoir of potential voters than older assumptions about the electorate would suggest.

The question is whether those voters show up.

Registration tells us who's on the roster. Polling tells us who's ahead. Turnout tells us who actually plays.

That's why a few points of registration movement, a presidential rally and the enthusiasm gap are all pieces of the same story.

And it's why the outcome remains so difficult to predict.

Now consider the mood of the country.

The latest Fox News poll finds that 74% rate the economy negatively. Sixty-six percent are dissatisfied with the direction of the country. Just 18% say their families are better off than two years ago.

Americans are unhappy. That's clear.

But unhappiness doesn't automatically tell us what they'll do.

Some angry voters become activists. Some become reliable voters. Some decide the whole system is hopeless and stop paying attention.

The same emotion can produce very different behavior.

And there's another complication.

Americans aren't particularly convinced that voting will solve their problems.

An October AP-NORC survey found roughly eight in 10 registered voters want Congress to prioritize lowering the cost of living.

Yet CBS finds that most voters don't expect their financial circumstances to improve regardless of which party wins.

Americans know exactly what they want fixed. They just don't have much confidence that either party will fix it.

That creates two competing forces.

Fear of what happens if the other side wins may drive people to the polls.

But frustration with both parties may convince some voters that the outcome won't make much difference.

Which force wins?

That's the question.

And the parties are spending an extraordinary amount of money trying to influence the answer.

Since Sept. 1, Democrats have spent more than $163 million on advertisements mentioning Trump. Republicans have spent approximately $11 million doing the same.

Democrats are spending nearly 15 times as much talking about Trump as Republicans are.

Apparently, Democrats have decided their most effective campaign spokesman is Donald Trump. Republicans seem considerably less enthusiastic about putting him in their advertisements.

But all that advertising is ultimately aimed at the same objective.

Get people to care enough to vote.

Early voting is already running ahead of the comparable point in 2022. More than 13 million early and mail ballots had been cast nationally by Oct. 22, compared with roughly 9 million at a similar point four years ago.

That sounds like a sign of enormous enthusiasm.

Maybe it is.

Or maybe people who would have voted on Election Day are simply voting earlier.

Early voting tells us that ballots are being cast. It doesn't necessarily tell us how many additional people will vote.

And it certainly doesn't tell us which party will benefit.

The same is true of outrage.

A country can be furious and still produce a surprisingly close election.

A party can dominate among the most motivated voters and still struggle if the other side's less enthusiastic supporters decide to participate.

And a candidate can win without persuading many people who weren't already inclined to vote for that candidate.

That's what makes this election so difficult to predict.

The most important voters may not be the ones changing their minds about Democrats or Republicans.

They may be the ones changing their minds about whether to bother voting at all.

Of course, the polls currently favor Democrats. The Fox News survey gives them a meaningful advantage. CBS projects they will reclaim the House.

Those are important findings, and they shouldn't be dismissed.

But a poll is a picture of an electorate. An election is an event in which some of those people participate and others don't.

The difference can be decisive.

So as we head into the final week, I'd pay less attention to the loudest voices and more attention to the people we aren't hearing from.

The occasional voter. The dissatisfied independent. The Republican who dislikes the direction of the country but isn't sure the Democrats would be better. The Democrat who fears Trump but isn't convinced Congress can change much.

These are the people who could decide the election.

Not necessarily because they've changed their minds about politics.

But because they may change their minds about participating.

The swing voter who changes parties gets all the attention. But the voter who swings between voting and staying home may decide this election.

And that's why Trump is on the road. Democrats are spending millions talking about him, and both parties are fighting over people who already agree with them.

The question isn't just which party Americans prefer.

It's which party can get its Americans to vote.

item.title: TSA finds sharp object straight out of horror movie at airport security checkpoint
item.description: TSA officers at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport spotted Wolverine-style claws on an X-ray, calling it the most unusual find they've made in two years.
item.content:encoded:
Officers conducting a routine security screening at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) uncovered a chilling object that seemed straight out of a horror movie.

While reviewing X-ray images, Transportation Security Administration (TSA) officers spotted a suspicious object that looked like a cross between Wolverine-style claws and Freddy Krueger blades, officials said.

"I saw three blades and distinct claw-like features," Officer Douglas Linn said in a report on the agency's website. "I was amazed, and even more so when it came out of the bag. I have never seen anything like this during my two years at TSA." 

SHARP WEAPON DISCOVERED BY TSA TUCKED INSIDE UNUSUAL ITEM IN PASSENGER'S CARRY-ON BAG

Officer Dennis Oishi, who was the property search officer, conducted a bag search and quickly confirmed there was a dangerous object inside.

The TSA shared an Instagram post about the object this week. Fox News Digital reached out to TSA for additional information.

What looked like a replica weapon from a movie set was quickly discovered.

"In my seven years with TSA, this is one of the most unusual items I have encountered. My first thought was, ‘Oh my gosh,’ and my second thought was, ‘Is this what I think it is?’" Responding Supervisory TSA Officer Ann Rhoades said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"When Dennis asked the passenger if there was anything sharp in the bag, he said he wasn’t sure. Obviously, there was," Rhoades added.

The passenger voluntarily removed the object from the bag.

"Officers Linn and Oishi demonstrated the vigilance, teamwork and professionalism that define TSA’s mission every day," said Robert Spinden, Seattle TSA's federal security director. 

"Their actions prevented a prohibited item from moving beyond the checkpoint and reinforced the importance of careful screening, clear coordination and calm execution," Spinden continued.

"I’m proud of their attention to detail and their commitment to keeping the traveling public safe."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The claw incident is not the first bizarre discovery made by TSA recently.

A routine security screening at upstate New York's Watertown International Airport (ART) took a startling turn when TSA officers discovered a spent smoke grenade hidden inside an aerosol container in a passenger's carry-on bag.

The discovery was made by TSA officers recently, according to a Sept. 24 release from the agency.

At Tampa International Airport, TSA officers discovered a 4-inch, double-edged knife concealed inside a baseball bat-shaped flashlight, the agency's website reported.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

TSA Officer Andrew Carter was screening the passenger's carry-on bag with an X-ray machine when he noticed something unusual about the flashlight and flagged the bag for a closer look.

"The makeup and composition of the flashlight appeared unusual and outside what I typically expect, so I determined it required further examination," Carter said in the published note.

Supervisory TSA Officer Michael Slaughter then searched the bag and felt a mass beneath its lining. After opening the lining, he found the baseball bat-shaped flashlight and noticed a line along its shaft.

"That is when it detached from the flashlight, revealing a 4-inch, double-edged knife integrated into the handle," he said.

Andrea Margolis and Kelly McGreal, both of Fox News Digital, contributed reporting.

item.title: Rays' comeback extra-innings victory in World Series Game 4 gives team kernel of hope, history shows
item.description: Ben Williamson's clutch 12th-inning single kept the Tampa Bay Rays alive in the World Series, but Jacob Misiorowski now looms large in Game 5.
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays entered Tuesday night in the worst position in sports – down 3-0 in the World Series with a nearly impossible hill to climb to achieve the improbable.

The Rays took care of business in Game 4, topping the Milwaukee Brewers in extra innings to pick up their first win of the series. Only one team in MLB history has come back to win a series being down 3-0 – the 2004 Boston Red Sox in the American League Championship Series against the New York Yankees. The Red Sox went on to win the title and end the "Curse of the Bambino."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Tampa Bay’s victory in Game 4 put the team in good company.

The Rays became the fourth team in World Series history to avoid elimination with an extra-inning comeback, according to Opta STATS. The franchise joined the 1912 Red Sox, 1986 New York Mets and 2011 St. Louis Cardinals. Each of those three teams won the World Series. However, none of those teams were ever down 3-0.

"We've got a lot of fight in us. We’re never going to shy away," Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson said. "We were going to keep fighting until the end — the last inning, the last out, the last play, the last pitch."

The Rays trailed 3-2 going into the bottom of the 12th. An error from the Brewers gave the Rays enough momentum to load the bases.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Ben Williamson came through in the clutch, hitting a single the other way and plating Nick Fortes.

"It just shows the resiliency of this group," Williamson said. "We continue to fight, and that’s been the motto this series and this full season, is just fight."

Winning Game 5 sure as hell isn’t going to be easy.

Two-time All-Star and National League Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski will take the bump for the Brewers. He allowed one run on four hits in five innings as the Brewers won Game 1.

Now, Misiorowski can send his team home happy or a little worried about a potential historic comeback.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Kathy Hochul 'excited' about prospect of Democrats tying Trump up in investigations
item.description: Kathy Hochul told Politico she's "excited" about Democrats using investigations and subpoenas to halt President Donald Trump's agenda if they retake Congress.
item.content:encoded:
Gov. Kathy Hochul, D-N.Y., told Politico Tuesday that she was "excited" at the possibility of a Democratic Congress holding up President Donald Trump's agenda through investigations and hearings.

Hochul brought up the concept while discussing the Democratic Party's chances of not only retaking the House in November, but the Senate as well. With both chambers of Congress, Hochul said Democrats could halt the "corruption" she alleged was occurring under the Trump administration.

"We are hoping for the House, but to get the Senate on top of it, next level, game-changing, extraordinary," Hochul said. "So, I'm excited about this. When you talk about Trump's next two years with that Democratic House and Senate, hey, guess what? There's investigations, there's hearings, there's subpoenas, there's questioning. We're putting the media spotlight on everything he's doing and trying to stop his 'flood the zone' strategy of doing so much bad stuff in such a short time that you can't even keep track of it."

THE NINE KEY RACES THAT WILL DECIDE WHO CONTROLS THE SENATE, AND WHERE THEY STAND

She added, "And so now you'll have congressional oversight committees and subcommittees and commissions. So that's going to tie things up to at least not that we want to stop the workings of the good part of government, but stop the corruption, stop the abuse and things that he's getting away with now. A fraction of them would have been national scandals for years and taken out here."

Despite her criticism of Trump's agenda, Hochul also voiced hope that she could work with the president in his final two years in office.

"I think there are some legacy projects that I've encouraged him to look at in New York as well. I want to build nuclear. I want to power this state with what'll ultimately be low-cost, reliable power," Hochul said.

GOV KATHY HOCHUL SIGNS NEW YORK ONTO TRUMP'S SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM DESPITE TEACHERS UNION OPPOSITION

She added, "I can do nuclear and look, I committed that we're going to build more nuclear in New York than the entire country has in the last 30 years. I need the president. I have a proposal before him now, how to unlock this and do it in half the time and much less cost. I've got a plan. So, those are areas where he can make a legacy in his home state."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said, "Democrats have no agenda to improve the lives of Americans—their only agenda is to continue their decade-long witch hunt against President Trump. This administration and commonsense Republicans will continue to secure our borders, restore law and order, putting more money back into the pockets of hard-working Americans, and deliver wins for the American people. The choice has never been clearer: doubling down on President Trump’s winning, commonsense agenda or the Democrats’ obstruction." 

BRUCE BLAKEMAN HAMMERS DEM GOV HOCHUL, MAMDANI OVER SUBWAY SAFETY DURING NYC CAMPAIGN RIDE

The New York Republican State Committee communications director David Laska criticized Hochul for saying the "quiet part out loud" and suggesting the Democrats' main goal is to halt the president's agenda rather than focus on the state.

"Kathy Hochul said the quiet part out loud, admitting that if Democrats win control of either chamber, they'll use the powers of Congress to thwart the President's agenda with phony hearings and investigations. Kathy Hochul should worry less about President Trump and more about the fact that New York continues to lead the nation in outmigration because she keeps us the most taxed, least affordable, least free state in the nation," Laska told Fox News Digital.

Hochul is up for re-election this November. She will face Republican nominee and Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman.

item.title: Attacker shouting 'Allahu Akbar' killed outside Israeli Embassy in Serbia, police say
item.description: An assailant shouting Allahu Akbar attacked a Gendarmerie officer outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade before being fatally shot by the officer.
item.content:encoded:
An assailant armed with two knives attacked a member of Serbia's Gendarmerie guarding the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight Wednesday, prompting the officer to fatally shoot the attacker in self-defense, according to Serbian authorities.

The assailant, who was a minor, allegedly shouted "Allahu Akbar" — or "God is great" in Arabic — as he slashed the officer in the face, leaving the officer "slightly injured."

Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said authorities are treating the incident as a terrorist attack, adding that security forces had been monitoring the assailant.

Dacic said the attacker supported ISIS and displayed a black flag bearing the terrorist group's symbol on his Instagram account. The attacker was believed to be Serbian and from the town of Sabac, Dacic added.

HALIMA SALMAN CONVICTED OF RECEIVING ISIS MILITARY TRAINING IN SYRIA, FACES 10 YEARS IN PRISON

Israel's foreign ministry confirmed the "attempted terrorist attack," and said the incident was under investigation by the relevant authorities.

"The attacker was neutralized by local police. No embassy personnel were injured, and the mission was closed at the time of the incident, which occurred late at night," the statement said.

According to Serbian prosecutors, an unidentified person wearing black clothes opened the door to the security booth outside the embassy around 12:15 a.m. local time.

FRANCE ON EDGE WITH 70,000 POLICE DEPLOYED FOR UNREST AS AUTHORITIES PROBE SUSPECTED TERROR ATTACK NEAR PARIS

Prosecutors said the attacker then walked toward the officer inside, identified as D.S., and threw one of his knives in his direction, hitting the officer in the left cheek.

D.S. then retrieved his service weapon and fired multiple rounds, killing the attacker on the spot, according to the office of the Higher Public Prosecutor in Belgrade.

Photos from the scene hours after the attack show heavily armed police officers standing at the entrance of the embassy.

Dacic said Serbia had raised its terrorism threat level to the highest level, prompting an increased police presence at sensitive sites and crowded public spaces across the country.

In June 2024, a crossbow-wielding assailant wounded a Serbian police officer guarding the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade before the officer returned fire, killing the attacker.

The latest attack comes a day after Israel held parliamentary elections, with exit polls pointing to no clear winner.

item.title: Collin Gosselin calls out reality TV producers for putting ratings ahead of kids: 'The show must go on'
item.description: Collin Gosselin's memoir alleges child exploitation on "Jon & Kate Plus 8," claiming production priorities came at the expense of his well-being.
item.content:encoded:
Collin Gosselin is sounding the alarm on the reality TV industry, accusing adults of turning a blind eye when children are hurting — all to keep the cameras rolling.

The "Jon & Kate Plus 8" star is revisiting the painful realities of his youth in his new memoir, "In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood," alleging that what made for compelling television often came at the expense of the children living it.

"It's the simple fact that adults that are seeing these things, they surely understood that people are choosing not to say anything because the show must go on," Collin told Fox News Digital.

'JON & KATE PLUS 8' STAR COLLIN GOSSELIN ACCUSES MOM OF TRYING TO 'BURY' HIM TO 'PROTECT HER REPUTATION'

"And if, at any point in time, a child can voice that they do not want to film, we need to take that seriously," he said.

Collin, one of the sextuplets who rose to fame alongside his parents and siblings, said children should not have to clearly articulate their distress before the adults around them recognize something is wrong.

"To understand and to know that at a young age, at any age, means that you really, you feel in your heart that it is not right, and you know you're being exploited and that's crazy for a child to know," he said. "But we should listen to that because that's a huge thing."

WATCH HERE: COLLIN GOSSELIN CALLS OUT REALITY TV PRODUCERS FOR PUTTING RATINGS AHEAD OF KIDS

Even when children remain silent, Collin argued, adults have a responsibility to pay attention.

"But even without a child saying anything, you can tell, you can absolutely tell. It's reading body language," Collin said. "You can absolutely tell and we should be aware. We should be paying attention. We should be protecting children."

WATCH: COLLIN GOSSELIN BLASTS MOM KATE FOR 'BURYING' HIM TO SAVE HER REPUTATION

Collin said the show's production priorities came at the expense of his well-being and that of his siblings, arguing that the demands of filming conflicted with what was best for the children.

"100% my entire childhood, what was best for production was this direct relationship to what was unhealthy for a child," he said. "But nobody cared about the welfare of me and my siblings, they cared about my paycheck."

He also said his siblings were kept in the dark about what happened at home while they were at school, adding that he hopes they will examine his account for themselves.

JON GOSSELIN CLAIMS HE'S 'PERFECT STRANGERS NOW' WITH SIX OF HIS KIDS AFTER YEARS OF NO CONTACT

"A lot happened that was kept from them intentionally so that they could be told that their brother was this and that," Collin said.

As filming intensified, Collin said the family's public image took priority over the children's experiences at home.

"But once everything got going, and we were at the height of filming and production, it was absolutely more about what it looked like on the outside and not necessarily how me and my siblings felt," he said. "It was always about how it looked for everybody else."

For Collin, the failure is not simply recognizing that something is wrong, but refusing to act.

"Doing something about it because the biggest thing is when we know something's wrong, and we don't say anything that's worse than not knowing it," he said.

Collin said the family that audiences watched on "Jon & Kate Plus 8" did not reflect the full reality of his childhood, arguing that viewers saw a more polished version of life at home.

KATE GOSSELIN CALLED A 'MONSTER' IN SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS AFTER SON COLLIN ANNOUNCES MEMOIR

When asked what cameras failed to capture, he described experiences and opportunities that he said were offered to the children for filming but later taken away.

His criticism goes beyond editing and production decisions. Collin also revisited his experience of being placed in a treatment facility and given medication, describing a period when he felt stripped of control over his life.

"For a long time, my name was dragged, and I was put away. I was essentially put in a juvenile prison, put on all these medications," he said. "I was a zombie half the time. I had no control, I had nothing."

WATCH: COLLIN GOSSELIN DETAILS ALLEGED ABUSE, CONFRONTS FAMILY TRAUMA

He said he spent that time doing what he was told, with little ability to change his circumstances.

"I did what I was told. I went through the motions, and was like a zombie every day," he said.

Reflecting on that experience, Collin said he feels compelled to speak publicly about what happened.

"And so when you reflect on all that, you realize these things need to be talked about, and I feel just an urge to talk about them," he said.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Collin said he has not spoken to his mother. He recalled a visit from Kate when he was 13, claiming the encounter left him with a painful final memory.

"She berated me for all of 20 minutes after not seeing me for over a year," he said.

Meanwhile, Collin told Fox News Digital he held on to hope even during what he described as his darkest moments.

"I had very little hope, but I always had some, and I hung on to that … I just kept telling myself that there's a better future for me and there will be a time where I will be past this," he said.

The former child star said sharing his story had weighed on him for years before he finally decided to speak publicly.

"It was heavy on my heart to tell my story and to hope that it would create change," he said.

As for reconciliation with his mother, Collin said an apology alone would not be enough to repair their relationship.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Reconciliation requires action and accountability," he said. "I think we can all say, I'm sorry, but if we're not willing to take the actions and take accountability for what has happened in the past and what happened my entire childhood, then what does that really mean, you know?"

"Jon & Kate Plus 8" followed Jon and Kate Gosselin as they raised their twin daughters, Mady and Cara, alongside their sextuplets: Collin, Alexis, Hannah, Aaden, Leah and Joel.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

The series aired from 2007 to 2009 before returning as "Kate Plus 8" in 2010. Following the couple's divorce, Collin was placed in a treatment facility as a child. He later moved in with his father, Jon Gosselin, after Jon obtained custody.

Collin's memoir, "In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood," is out now.

item.title: Watchdog accuses DSA candidate of blurring charity, business and campaign: ‘What happened to all that money?’
item.description: The NLPC complaint alleges Angie Nixon's Moxie Group nonprofit left $210,000 in spending unaccounted for as she campaigns for Florida Senate.
item.content:encoded:
The National Legal and Policy Center (NLPC), a conservative government watchdog, filed a complaint on Monday against Angie Nixon, a state legislator and candidate for U.S. Senate in Florida backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), alleging that she may have violated "a number of Florida and federal laws."

The complaint asks authorities to probe whether she used her now-defunct nonprofit, the Moxie Group Inc., to benefit herself. It comes as Nixon wages an uphill race to unseat Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla.

Nixon's campaign disputes the characterizations, noting that Nixon's involvement with the nonprofit ended in December 2025 when she resigned as its principal manager. The Moxie Group was initially intended to receive federal tax-exempt contributions for a community project named Café Resistance, a community-oriented bookstore and coffee shop in Jacksonville.

NLPC is asking the Federal Election Commission, the IRS, the U.S. Attorney’s Office and the Florida attorney general to investigate the Moxie Group along four lines: unaccounted-for charitable expenses, overlap between the nonprofit and a for-profit business, whether it solicited donations even after the group was disbanded and whether Nixon’s use of her business space for campaign purposes violates federal campaign restrictions.

DEFEATED PROGRESSIVE ‘SQUAD’ LAWMAKER IN HOT SEAT FOR NON-PROFIT’S MISSING PAPER TRAIL

According to the Moxie Group’s 2024 reporting, it spent $210,000 with an "other" designation, leaving most of its spending unaccounted for.

"While she itemized some of the charity’s expenses … a whopping $210,000 ... was simply listed as ‘other’ with no description or itemization of what those funds were spent for even though the form requires the charity to ‘list item’ for those ‘other’ expenses. What happened to all that money?" NLPC wrote in its complaint.

Parts of the $210,000 figure have broad descriptions but lack itemization in the 2024 reporting. Two of them under the "other" designation include one $42,560 payment and another $68,304 disbursement, both under "program services." A third, a $3,437 item, is categorized under "management & general."

Outside the "other" category, listed expenses include equipment rentals, insurance, advertising, information technology and fees for non-employees.

The unknowns in the money trail, NLPC contends, are especially important given the overlap between Nixon’s nonprofit and her business — the complaint’s second area of concern.

The document notes that after founding her nonprofit in 2019, Nixon transferred its registration license to her personal for-profit company by the same name — DBA Café Resistance Bookstore and Coffee Shop.

SENATE HOPEFUL'S 'TREADING WATER' NARRATIVE CRUMBLES UNDER $500K CAMPAIGN PAYOUTS TO FAMILY

"Although the charity was ostensibly established to raise funds for a local community bookstore/café, the license for that establishment was transferred to her for-profit The Moxie Group LLC DBA Café Resistance Bookstore and Coffee Shop," the complaint reads.

Third, NLPC questioned whether Nixon raised donations for her nonprofit even after its board of directors voted to disband the group on Dec. 15, 2025.

"It waited over nine months to file Articles of Dissolution with the Florida Secretary of State on Oct. 1, 2026," the group wrote.

The complaint says the Moxie Group did not take down its fundraising site, stating that its contributors were promised "a tax receipt for making a donation," a confirmation for charitable donations. The complaint includes screenshots of the now-archived website.

Fox News Digital is not aware of any specific contributions the Moxie Group may have received that were directed to the nonprofit during that time. Nixon's campaign noted that, because she stepped down as the nonprofit's manager in December 2025 — ahead of the board's disbandment on Dec. 15 — she would not have been involved in any decisions about the group's articles of dissolution or donations received after her resignation.

As its final area of concern, NLPC believes that previously reported accounts of letting the group use its space for campaign events — without some form of payment — would constitute a violation of campaign finance laws.

"It appears that the Café Resistance and Bookstore has been functioning as the candidate’s campaign de facto headquarters or a branch thereof. Indeed, Café Resistance is hosting a phone bank operation on its premises," the complaint states.

According to Nixon’s campaign website, the coffee shop is listed as the location for "Ten toes down Tuesday phonebank," an event scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 27.

"Let’s go all in for Angie!! Tuesdays can be so fun when we spend them phonebanking for Angie! Together we will call registered voters to remind them that early voting is going on statewide and we need them to vote, now more than ever! Bring your charged-up phone, laptops and/or tablets!" the event’s description reads.

Nixon’s campaign said it has not made payments to Café Resistance and has used only the group’s parking lot. The campaign also noted that Nixon does not own the building.

Even so, NLPC also noted that if any of the funding that had been made as a contribution to the nonprofit had ended up paying for the business’ rent, that could also constitute a campaign finance violation, the group contends.

SENATE REPUBLICAN SETTLES SIX-YEAR-OLD CAMPAIGN BILL AFTER BEING CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA

"To the extent that contributions to the charity were used to pay the rent and expenses of the for-profit Café Resistance Bookstore and Coffee Shop, which in turn was used for Angie Nixon’s political campaign, that is a clear violation of 501(c)(3) rules that prohibit charities from using their funds for political campaign purposes," the document reads.

Having secured the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate earlier this year, Nixon will face off against Moody next week in the state's Nov. 3 general election.

item.title: Apple News pushed 84 negative headlines about GOP priorities ahead of midterms with zero positive, study finds
item.description: The MRC study found Apple News promoted 84 negative headlines on Republican priorities and zero positive ones during the lead-up to midterm elections.
item.content:encoded:
Apple News promoted more than 80 stories that negatively framed the issues Republicans care about during the lead-up to the midterm elections while promoting zero positive stories about GOP-aligned issues, according to the Media Research Center (MRC).

The MRC, a conservative media watchdog, analyzed Apple News’ top 20 stories from Sept. 15-30 and found that voters who rely on the platform for information were fed roughly five stories per day that negatively characterized the Republicans' top 10 policy priorities.

During that same period, Apple News, which comes preinstalled on every iPhone in America, did not promote a single story that positively framed a Republican priority, according to the study.

APPLE, GOOGLE NEWS ALGORITHMS SUPPRESSED NEGATIVE STORIES ON MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL EL-SAYED, STUDY SAYS

"Apple News ran 84 negative headlines on Republican priorities and zero positive ones. Zero! My dentist finds more good news in a root canal," David Bozell told Fox News Digital.

"Millions of voters open that app before they vote, and Apple's editors are in there like a bartender who waters down only one party's drinks," David Bozell continued. "Come on, Apple, tell us who picks these stories and why Republicans got the whole bad-news buffet."

MRC staffers Luis Cornelio and Madison Van Zant, who conducted the study, wrote that their findings add to the "growing body of evidence that the platform’s editors continue to curate its feeds to push a left-wing political agenda."

The MRC found that 117 stories from outlets Apple News promoted GOP-aligned issues during the review period, with 84 stories featuring negative headlines (72%) and 33 (28%) receiving neutral headlines. None of the headlines promoted by Apple News presented GOP issues in a positive light.

APPLE AND GOOGLE SUPPRESSED NEGATIVE GRAHAM PLATNER STORIES FOR MONTHS ON THEIR NEWS PLATFORM, STUDY FINDS

"In short, Apple News ensured that immigration was framed through court defeats and sensationalist stories; the economy through high gas prices; law and order through positive portrayals of police abolition; cuts to government through accusations of radicalism; foreign policy through portrayals of America’s adversaries as warriors; and efforts to curb waste through claims of unlawful cuts," Cornelio and Van Zant wrote.

The study was conducted after the MRC identified 10 prominent Republican-aligned issues based on recent polls: immigration and border security, the economy, law and order, reducing government spending, combating drug use, national security and foreign policy, taxes, countering terrorism, education and protecting the unborn.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Apple News has long been accused of having a liberal bias, and Fox News Digital reported earlier this year that many of the company’s top executives and board members have made substantial contributions to Democrats over multiple election cycles.

Some conservatives were hopeful that Apple News would pivot once new CEO John Ternus took control of the company, but a previous MRC study found that the news aggregator increased the percentage of stories from leftist outlets during his first month on the job.

Apple did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Cheesecake Factory among list of popular eateries in America's priciest neighborhoods
item.description: Cava, Shake Shack and The Cheesecake Factory top a new analysis ranking restaurant chains by home values near their locations nationwide.
item.content:encoded:
The Cheesecake Factory has been in the headlines after former President Barack Obama joked that President Donald Trump's White House décor looked "like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory." 

The remark sparked debate over whether the chain is a spot for everyday Americans, and a new analysis of restaurant chains near neighborhoods with higher and lower home values found where it ranks.

Home values near Cheesecake Factory restaurants were about 27% higher than in areas in the same region with similar population density, partly because many of them are located in upscale malls, The Washington Sun found. 

5 RESTAURANT CHAINS SERVE UP THE BEST BREAKFAST VALUE AS AMERICANS LOOK TO SAVE

The outlet analyzed data from Overture Maps, Zillow and the Census Bureau using a methodology adapted from housing expert Aziz Sunderji's analysis of businesses near areas with higher and lower home values.

It traces its roots back to 2006, when three childhood friends opened a Greek restaurant honoring their shared heritage. They began selling dips in grocery stores in 2008 and launched the fast-casual chain in 2011. 

BELOVED RESTAURANT CHAIN DWINDLES FROM 850 LOCATIONS TO 87, BUT EXPERT SEES 'A LOT OF LIFE LEFT'

Cava celebrated its 500th store opening in September, according to a news release.

Home values near Shake Shacks were 38% higher than in similar areas. The burger chain began in 2001 as a hot dog cart in New York City's Madison Square Park, launched by restaurateur Danny Meyer's Union Square Hospitality Group to support a public art project.

"We certainly didn't invent them — but as a category, they now seem to be everywhere," Meyer told Eater last year.

The Cheesecake Factory's roots were in Beverly Hills, California, where David Overton opened the first restaurant in 1978 to showcase his mother Evelyn's cheesecakes. 

She began baking cheesecakes in Detroit in the 1940s before opening a small bakery in Los Angeles in 1972.

Decades later, it ranked third among restaurant chains in the analysis and has expanded to about 250 restaurants worldwide. 

BABY BOOMERS CROWN THEIR FAVORITE CASUAL DINING CHAIN AS GEN Z CHOOSES A DIFFERENT WINNER

It has also cemented its place in American culture, synonymous with the suburban mall experience of the 1990s and 2000s and a symbol of American excess with its large portions, sprawling menu and over-the-top interior design.

P.F. Chang's ranked fourth among the restaurant chains, with home values within three miles of its locations 26% higher than in comparable areas. 

The Asian-inspired chain is known for dishes such as Chicken Lettuce Wraps and Mongolian Beef and is similarly tied to the casual-dining boom of the 1990s and 2000s. 

Like The Cheesecake Factory, it serves generous portions and is a fixture in malls and shopping centers, with similarly elaborate decor.

Chipotle Mexican Grill and Panera Bread tied for fifth, with home values within three miles of both chains' locations 17% higher than in comparable areas.

item.title: Poll shows Hochul adding to lead over Blakeman in New York governor's race: 'Running out of time'
item.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul leads Bruce Blakeman by 14 points in a Siena poll, but a plurality of voters say neither will make life more affordable.
item.content:encoded:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul expanded her lead over Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman to double digits in a new poll showing the Democratic incumbent pulling further ahead in the final days before Election Day.

Hochul leads the Nassau County executive 54% to 40% among likely New York voters, according to a Siena Research Institute survey released Wednesday. The 14-point margin is five points wider than her lead in September, when she led 50% to 41%.

"Heading into the final stretch, Hochul has a 14-point lead, with Blakeman quickly running out of time to close a gap that is growing rather than narrowing," Siena pollster Steven Greenberg said in a statement.

NEW YORK GOVERNOR DEBATE HEATS UP AS BLAKEMAN, HOCHUL SPAR OVER TRUMP, SANCTUARY STATUS, ICE SHOOTING

The poll also showed Blakeman struggling to establish an advantage in areas where Republicans typically need strong support to compete statewide. The candidates are virtually tied in upstate New York and the downstate suburbs, while Hochul leads independent voters by 11 points.

Republicans generally need strong margins in those regions and among independents to overcome Democrats' roughly two-to-one voter registration advantage and their dominance in New York City, Greenberg noted.

"But with only a week to go, Blakeman and Hochul are running virtually evenly upstate and in the downstate suburbs, while Hochul has an 11-point lead with independents," Greenberg said, noting that Blakeman is "quickly running out of time to close a gap that is growing rather than narrowing."

Despite Hochul's overall advantage, the survey revealed uncertainty among voters over whether either candidate would make life more affordable for average New Yorkers.

DEBRA MESSING SAYS COST OF LIVING, SUBWAY VIOLENCE PUSHED HER TO BACK TRUMP-ENDORSED REPUBLICAN

A plurality of voters, 35%, said neither candidate would make life more affordable, compared with 30% who chose Hochul and 27% who selected Blakeman.

Hochul also reached a new milestone in the survey, with 51% of likely voters viewing her favorably compared with 45% who viewed her unfavorably. It marked the first time a majority of voters had viewed her favorably in Siena polling during her five years as governor.

Her job approval rating also rose to 51%, up from 48% in September. Blakeman, meanwhile, received a 39% favorable rating and a 40% unfavorable rating.

The survey found a sizable gender gap, with Hochul leading Blakeman by 23 points among women and six points among men. She also led among Black voters, 81% to 16%, while White voters were closely divided.

The poll also found that 68% of likely voters believed Hochul would win the election, compared with 23% who predicted a Blakeman victory. Among Republicans surveyed, 40% said they expected Hochul to win.

In New York's other statewide races, Democratic Attorney General Letitia James led Republican Saritha Komatireddy 54% to 39%, while Democratic state Comptroller Tom DiNapoli led Republican Joseph Hernandez 59% to 32%.

The Siena poll was conducted Oct. 19–22 among 807 likely New York voters through telephone and text-to-web surveys. It has a margin of error of plus or minus 4.1 percentage points.

Election Day is Nov. 3.

item.title: Real Madrid issues apology to China over Mbappe controversy after state-run TV demands it
item.description: Real Madrid issued a formal apology to China after CCTV demanded one, reversing its initial defense of Kylian Mbappe's freedom of expression.
item.content:encoded:
Real Madrid stood firm longer than most clubs would – all of a few hours – before bending the knee to China and issuing a formal apology amid the controversy and backlash involving forward Kylian Mbappe and a meme of the late dictator Mao Zedong.

The club initially argued that Mbappe had no intent to offend while also explaining that players have freedom of expression, which predictably did not go over well.

During a recent interview on The Bridge, a French talk show hosted by Mbappe's Real Madrid teammate Aurelien Tchouameni, the 27-year-old superstar laughed about a meme with his face imposed on an image resembling Mao. One of Mbappe's most popular nicknames is "The Dictator," hence the meme and joking around.

China did not find anything funny about the French star laughing at a meme of Mao, the communist dictator whose regime resulted in tens of millions of deaths. Several Chinese sponsors severed ties with Mbappe, and state-run CCTV stopped airing La Liga matches in China, the top-flight league in Spain that featured Real Madrid and 19 other clubs.

La Liga wasted no time in issuing a public apology, explaining that Mbappe's comments do not represent the league. Less than an hour later came Mbappe's own public apology, which included a note that he now understands his comments "hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world."

BOBBY BURACK: KYLIAN MBAPPÉ JOINS LEBRON JAMES, JOHN CENA, OTHER ATHLETES IN BENDING THE KNEE TO CHINA

Real Madrid did not follow suit with a public bending of the knee to China until Wednesday, that is, after immense pressure from state-run media.

The Spanish giant tried distancing itself from Mbappe's comments, a virtually impossible endeavor given Mbappe is among the most popular athletes in the world, by releasing comments to Spanish news outlet Okdiario.

According to the outlet, the club did not believe Mbappe's "personal expression" would affect commercial connections in China, nor did it believe he had any intent to offend the Chinese people.

CCTV did not appreciate Real Madrid's initial response, and issued a statement explaining that it did "not accept this attitude" from the club and that until it issues an apology, "all other discussions are off-limits."

Real Madrid wasted no time and issued a public apology very shortly after CCTV demanded it.

"Real Madrid C.F. wishes to apologize to the Chinese people for any distress that may have been caused by the recent remarks made by our player, Kylian Mbappé," the apology began.

"Our club holds deep respect for China — its history, its culture, and its citizens—as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid."
